verdicts.reason: Quote states shared i_clk_core, rising edge, no gating. Scenario check (clock connectivity) is plausible.

Structural requirement on the design; the bridge/RTL is the actor. Nothing is observable at interface as a runtime check, so check none is fine, but actor should be the bridge not the system... keeping check none.
Quote states the FIFO clock and reset tie-offs; structural connectivity, not simulation-checkable.

Reset values are checkable from interface signals while i_rst_n_core is low (HREADYOUT, HRESP, VALIDs, BREADY/RREADY). FIFO valid state is internal, but the interface outputs are assertable. Keep as assertion; actor is the bridge, not system.
Quote states the SoC provides a single reset net with async assertion and synchronized deassertion; integration requirement, not checkable at the IP.
Quote states RTL uses i_rst_n_core directly with no reset synchronizer; structural.

Quote 'No transaction is accepted until reset release' is checkable at the interface (no HREADYOUT-accepted transfer / no AXI handshakes during reset). Actor is the bridge acting as AHB slave; assertion is acceptable.
Quote states the system shall reset the AXI endpoint/interconnect consistently; a system-level integration requirement.

questions.question: AA-7.3-01 lists 'FIFO valid state cleared' as a reset value, but this is internal. Should verification check it via hierarchical probes or only via the interface outputs?

AA-7.3-04 says no transaction is accepted until reset release. Is acceptance defined as HREADYOUT high with HTRANS active, or as any AXI handshake? What is the first cycle after release where a transfer may be accepted?
